long_biography.plain_text:
Claus Groepper brought American country music to German television through Country Time, a programme hosted by Freddy Quinn. He conceived it as a ninety-minute annual special, with his Ifage production company making the shows for ZDF. Its audience extended into Austria and Switzerland, and the format developed into six broadcasts a year.

Groepper brought session musicians from Nashville to accompany visiting American singers. The performances were recorded live in concert halls, without overdubbing, then edited into shorter television programmes. Quinn presented in both English and German. Working with Nashville producer Brien Fisher, Groepper broadened the guest list from traditional country performers towards crossover artists.
